diagrams.caption: Black 7 takes the ko, and White 8 retakes after a threat elsewhere. Black 9 is a local threat; White 10 answers it, and Black 11 retakes with no threat elsewhere. White has no second threat and plays elsewhere with White 12; Black 13 connects and White is dead.
If White 10 connects the ko instead of answering Black 9, Black 11 kills; White's outside liberty at A16 does not help.
Played before the ko is taken, the exchange of Black 7 for White 8 spends Black's threat. After Black 9 takes the ko, it is a plain KO+.

text: Black 7 in Diagram 2 takes the ko first, which alone would give KO+. Every local White answer dies, so White must retake after a threat elsewhere. But then Black 9 is a local ko threat: if White ignores it and connects the ko, Black 11 in Diagram 3 kills. So White 10 in Diagram 2 must answer, and Black 11 retakes without spending an outside threat. White dies there although it had one threat more than Black.

White has no local threat to cancel Black's threat at A19; both reviewers looked and found none. So White needs two more ko threats than Black to live: S[KO+2]. The threat must be at A19: White's outside liberty at A16 means a threat at B19 does not work. Black must also keep it in reserve: played before the ko is taken, it leaves a plain KO+ (Diagram 4).

The solver confirms each step, both reviewers agree, and the site's tutorial counts local threats in the label. Some searches in a wider area stayed undecided, but those positions die in the solver's search area and by the reviewers' reading.
